paragraphs: Let me say this plainly, friend: death is heavy, and this passage treats it that way. Whoever touches a dead body is unclean for seven days (Num 19:11), and whatever the unclean person touches becomes unclean too (Num 19:22). It spreads like flour on my counter. One little puff and it's on EVERYTHING. The LORD is teaching Israel that uncleanness has to be taken seriously, because it could defile the tabernacle of the LORD (Num 19:13).

But here's the part I LOVE, friend. God doesn't leave anybody stuck in that mess. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer under the dust, so trust me, I know how stuck feels. He gave a way back: water made with the ashes of the sin offering, for purification from sin (Num 19:9, 17). And nobody could shrug it off or just wait it out, because the person who did not purify himself was cut off (Num 19:20).

Hebrews 9:13-14 says the ashes of a heifer sprinkled on those made unclean made their bodies clean, and that the blood of Christ does so much more, cleansing our consciences from dead works so that we may serve the living God. So here's the takeaway, baker: don't hide your mess, bring it to the One who made the way to be clean. My ovens stay ready, so come as you are and let's get baking!
